question: What was God’s response to the sun, moon, and stars he created on the fourth day?

question: What did God do on the seventh day?

question: What was the snake’s first question to Eve?

question: What did God say would happen if Adam and his wife ate from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil?

question: What did the snake say was the reason God did not want them to eat the fruit?

question: Why did the woman eat the fruit?

question: Were Adam and his wife forced to eat the fruit?

question: What did the man and the woman do when they realized they were naked?

question: How did the man respond when God confronted him about his sin?

question: How did the woman respond when God confronted her about her sin?

question: What was God’s curse on the snake?

question: What was God’s curse on the woman?

question: What was God’s curse on the man?
answer: You will work hard to grow food, and you will die and return to the soil.

question: How did God prevent Adam and Eve from living forever?

question: Why did God decide to destroy the world?

question: How did God plan to destroy the world?

question: Why kind of man was Noah?
answer: He was a righteous man.

question: What did God tell Noah to do?
answer: God told him to build a huge boat.

question: What was the purpose of the boat?

question: How did the other people react when Noah told them that the flood would come?

question: Which animals came into the boat before the flood?

question: Who closed the door of the boat after Noah’s family and the animals came inside?
answer: God closed the door.

question: How long did it rain?
answer: It rained for 40 days and 40 nights.

question: How high did the water of the flood reach?

question: What happened to everything that lived on land?
answer: Everything died.

question: How did Noah know the water had dried up?

question: What did God tell Noah and his family to do when they left the boat?
answer: He told them to have many children and grandchildren and to fill the earth.

question: How did Noah worship God after he got off the boat?
answer: He built an altar and sacrificed some of the animals.

question: What did God promise he would never do again?
answer: He would never again curse the ground or destroy the world with a flood.

question: What did God make as a sign of his promise?
answer: He made a rainbow in the sky.

question: After the flood, did the people fill the earth as God had commanded?
answer: No, they gathered together and built a city.

question: How many different languages were there in the world at that time?
answer: There was only one language.

question: What did the people work together to do instead of spreading out over the earth?
answer: They started to build a tall tower that would reach heaven.

question: What did God do to cause the people to spread out all over the world?
answer: He changed their language into many different languages.

question: What was the name of the city that they were building?
answer: It was named **Babel**.

question: What does the name **Babel** mean?
answer: It means ‘confused.’

question: What did God tell Abram to do?
answer: God told Abram to leave his country and family and go to another land.

question: What did God promise to do for Abram?
answer: He promised to give Abram all the land he could see, to make his name great, to make his descendants a great nation, and to bless all the families on earth through him.

question: To which land did Abram go?
answer: He went to the land of Canaan.

question: What promise did God make to Abram about Canaan?
answer: God would give it to Abram and his descendants would always possess it.

question: Who was Melchizedek?
answer: He was the priest of God Most High.

question: What did Melchizedek do for Abram?
answer: He blessed Abram.

question: What did Abram give to Melchizedek?
answer: He gave him a tenth of all he owned.

question: What did God promise Abram after he had lived in Canaan for many years?
answer: Abram would have a son and as many descendants as the stars in the sky.

question: Why did God say Abram was righteous?
answer: He said this because Abram believed God’s promise.

question: What is a covenant?
answer: A covenant is an agreement between two parties.

question: Why did Sarai think she would not have children?
answer: She was too old.

question: What did Sarai tell Abram to do in order to have a child?
answer: Marry her servant Hagar, so Hagar could have a child for her.

question: What was the name of Hagar’s child?
answer: His name was **Ishmael**.

question: What problem happened between Sarai and Hagar?
answer: Sarai became jealous of Hagar.

question: What covenant promises did God make to Abram?
answer: Abram would be the father of many nations, and God would give the land of Canaan to him and to his descendants.

question: What did God tell Abram to do as a sign of the covenant between them?
answer: Abram must circumcise every male in his family.

question: Who did God say would be the son of the promise?
answer: Isaac, Sarai’s son, would be the son of promise.

question: Who did God say would become a great nation?
answer: Both Isaac and Ishmael would become great nations.

question: What did Abram’s new name, Abraham, mean?
answer: His name means **father of many**.

question: What did God ask Abraham to do to Isaac when Isaac was a young man?
answer: God asked Abraham to sacrifice Isaac to him.

question: Why did God ask Abraham to sacrifice Isaac?
answer: God did this to test Abraham’s faith.

question: What did Abraham tell Isaac was the reason they did not have a lamb for the sacrifice?
answer: Abraham said God would provide the lamb for the sacrifice.

question: Did God want Abraham to kill Isaac?
answer: No, he only wanted to see if Abraham would obey him.

question: What did God provide as a sacrifice instead of Isaac?
answer: He provided a ram stuck in a bush.

question: What did God promise to do for Abraham because Abraham had obeyed him?
answer: He promised that Abraham’s descendents would be more than the stars in the sky, and that all the families of the world would be blessed through his family.

question: Why did Abraham send his servant back to the land of Abraham’s relatives?
answer: He sent him to bring back a wife for his Abraham’s son, Isaac.

question: How did the servant find Rebekah?
answer: God led him to her.

question: How was Rebekah related to Abraham?
answer: Rebekah was the granddaughter of Abraham’s brother.

question: Was Rebekah forced to go with the servant to marry Isaac?
answer: No, she agreed to go.

question: What promises of God were passed on to Isaac when Abraham died?
answer: All of the promises that God had made to Abraham, including that he would have countless descendants, were passed on to Isaac.

question: Why did it appear that the promise of countless descendants would not be fulfilled through Isaac?
answer: Rebekah could not have children.

question: What did God tell Rebekah about her two twin sons before they were born?
answer: They would become two nations, and the older son will serve the younger one.

question: What was the name of the older son?
answer: His name was **Esau**.

question: What was the name of the younger son?
answer: His name was **Jacob**.

question: Esau was the older son. Why did he give everything that he should receive to Jacob, the younger son?
answer: Everything Esau should have received as the older son, he gave Jacob in exchange for some food.

question: To whom did Isaac want to give his formal blessing?
answer: He gave it to Esau.

question: How did Jacob trick Isaac into giving him the blessing?
answer: He pretended to be Esau by wearing goatskins so that Isaac would think he was Esau.

question: Because Jacob stole Esau’s blessing, what did Esau plan to do to him?
answer: Esau planned to kill Jacob after Isaac died.

question: What did Isaac and Rebekah do when Rebekah heard of Esau’s plan to kill Jacob?
answer: They sent Jacob far away to live with Rebekah’s relatives.

question: What happened to Jacob during the next twenty years?
answer: He married, had 12 sons and a daughter, and God made him wealthy.

question: Why was Jacob afraid when he returned to Canaan?
answer: He thought Esau would kill him.

question: What did Jacob do in order to soothe Esau’s anger?
answer: He sent herds of animals to Esau as a gift.

question: Was Esau still angry with Jacob?
answer: No, he no longer wanted to harm Jacob.

question: Where did Jacob settle to live?
answer: He settled in Canaan.

question: After Isaac’s death, who received the covenant promises that God originally gave to Abraham?
answer: Jacob received them.

question: Why did Joseph’s brothers hate him?
answer: Because Joseph was Jacob’s favorite son, and because Joseph had dreamed he would be their ruler.

question: What evil thing did Joseph’s brothers do to him?
answer: They took him captive and sold him to some slave traders.

question: How did Joseph’s brothers explain his disappearance to Jacob?
answer: They put goat’s blood on Joseph’s robe so that Jacob would think a wild animal had killed him.

question: Did God abandon Joseph in Egypt?
answer: No, in everything Joseph did, God blessed him.

question: Why was Joseph sent to prison in Egypt?
answer: Joseph refused to sleep with his master’s wife, so she falsely accused him.

question: What ability had God given Joseph?
answer: He gave him the ability to interpret dreams.

question: What was the meaning of Pharaoh’s dream?
answer: God was going to send seven years of plentiful harvests followed by seven years of famine.

question: How did Pharaoh reward Joseph after Joseph interpreted his dream?
answer: He made Joseph the second most powerful man in Egypt.

question: How did Joseph prepare for the famine?
answer: Joseph told the Egyptians to store up large amounts of food during the seven good years, and then he sold the food to the people during the seven years of famine.

question: Why did Joseph’s brothers come to Egypt?
answer: They came to buy food because the famine was severe in Canaan also.

question: Before Joseph told his brothers who he was, why did he test them?
answer: He tested them to see if they had changed.

question: How did God cause good to come from Joseph’s brothers selling him as a slave?
answer: Joseph became a powerful ruler in Egypt, and God used him to provide food for his family and many other people during the famine.

question: What did Jacob do after he found out that Joseph was alive?
answer: He moved his whole family to Egypt.

question: After Jacob died, who received the promises that God gave to Abraham?
answer: The 12 sons of Jacob received them.

question: What did the descendants of the 12 sons of Jacob become?
answer: They became the 12 tribes of Israel.

question: Why were the Egyptians afraid of the Israelites?
answer: They were afraid because there were so many Israelites.

question: What did Pharaoh do to the Israelites because he was afraid of them?
answer: He made them slaves to the Egyptians.

question: How did Pharaoh try to keep the Israelites from increasing in number?
answer: He ordered all Israelite baby boys to be thrown into the Nile River.

question: What happened to the baby boy in the basket in the river?
answer: A daughter of Pharaoh saw him, took him as her own son, and named him Moses.

question: What did Moses do in order to save a fellow Israelite?
answer: He killed an Egyptian who was beating him, and buried the Egyptian’s body.

question: Why did Moses have to flee from Egypt?
answer: When Pharaoh found out that he killed the Egyptian, he wanted to kill Moses.

question: Where did Moses go to escape from Pharaoh?
answer: He went to the wilderness.

question: What unusual thing did Moses see while taking care of his sheep in the wilderness?
answer: He saw a bush that was on fire, but it did not burn up.

question: What did God tell Moses as he approached the burning bush?
answer: God said, “Moses, take off your shoes. You are standing on holy ground.”

question: How do we know God cared about the Israelites in Egypt?
answer: God said to Moses, “I have seen the suffering of my people.”

question: What did God send Moses to do for the Israelites?
answer: God told him to go to Pharaoh and bring the Israelites out of their slavery in Egypt.

question: What land did God say he would give to the Israelites?
answer: God would give him the land of Canaan, the land God had promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

question: What name did God say would be his forever?
answer: He said his name would be Yahweh.

question: Who did God send to help Moses?
answer: God sent Moses’ brother, Aaron, to help him.

question: What was God’s message that Moses and Aaron gave to Pharaoh?
answer: God’s message to Pharaoh was, “Let my people go!”

question: What did Pharaoh do when he heard this command?
answer: He forced the Israelites to work even harder.

question: What did God do when Pharaoh refused to let the Israelites go?
answer: He sent ten terrible plagues on Egypt.

question: What did God show Pharaoh through these plagues?
answer: He showed that he is more powerful than Pharaoh and all of Egypt’s gods.

question: What did God do to the water in the Nile River?
answer: God turned water in the Nile River into blood.

question: Who was affected by the plague of the painful skin sores?
answer: The sores appeared on the Egyptians, but not on the Israelites.

question: Did the plague of darkness affect everyone equally?
answer: No, it was dark where the Egyptians lived, but there was light where the Israelites lived.

question: How did Pharaoh respond to each of the first nine plagues?
answer: He refused to let the people go free.

question: What did God do after Pharaoh did not respond to the first nine plagues?
answer: God planned to send one last plague.

question: What would this last plague do that the first nine had not done?
answer: It would change Pharaoh’s mind.

question: What did God say he would do to the Egyptians if Pharaoh did not let the Israelites go?
answer: He would kill all the firstborn males of both people and animals.

question: How could people save their firstborn son?
answer: They had to kill a perfect lamb.

question: What did God tell the Israelites to do with the blood of the lamb?
answer: God told them to put the blood of the lamb around the door of their house.

question: What specific food did God tell the Israelites to eat with the roasted lamb?
answer: They were to eat bread that was made without yeast.

question: What were the Israelites to be ready to do when they ate?
answer: They were to be ready to leave Egypt.

question: What did God do at the houses that had the blood around the doors?
answer: He passed over those houses and everyone inside was safe.

question: What did God do at every Egyptian house?
answer: He killed the firstborn son.

question: How many of the firstborn sons of the Egyptians were killed?
answer: All of them died, including Pharaoh’s son.

question: What did Pharaoh tell Moses and Aaron after this plague?
answer: He told them to take the Israelites and leave Egypt immediately!

question: What did the Egyptians give the Israelites as they left Egypt?
answer: They gave them whatever they asked for, even gold and silver and other valuable things.

question: Who else left Egypt with the Israelites?
answer: Some people from other nations who believed in God left with them.

question: How did God lead the Israelites?
answer: He led them in a pillar of cloud during the day and a pillar of fire at night.

question: Why did God cause Pharaoh to be stubborn and chase the Israelites?
answer: God did this to show that he is is the One True God who is more powerful than Pharaoh and his gods.

question: How did the Israelites react when they were trapped between the sea and Pharaoh’s army?
answer: They said, “Why did we leave Egypt? We are going to die!”

question: What did Moses say to the Israelites to calm their fear?
answer: He told them to stop being afraid! God would fight for them that day and save them.

question: How did God prevent the Egyptians from coming near the Israelites as they started to escape?
answer: He placed the pillar of cloud between them.

question: What did God tell Moses to do in order to make a path of escape for the Israelites?
answer: God told him to raise his hand over the sea so that the waters would divide.

question: How were the Israelites able to cross the sea?
answer: They walked through it on dry ground.

question: What happened to the Egyptians as they chased the Israelites through the sea?
answer: He caused the Egyptians to panic and their chariots to get stuck.

question: How did God destroy the Egyptian army?
answer: The water covered the Egyptian army so that they drowned.

question: How did the Israelites react when they saw that the Egyptians were dead?
answer: They trusted in God and believed that Moses was a prophet of God.

question: Why did the Israelites sing and praise God?
answer: They praised him because he had saved them from the Egyptians.

question: What did God tell the Israelites to do in order to remember his victory over the Egyptians?
answer: He commanded them to celebrate the Passover every year.

question: Where did God lead the Israelites after they crossed the Red Sea?
answer: He lead them to a mountain called Sinai.

question: What did God promise the Israelites that they would become if they would obey him?
answer: They would be his prized possession, a kingdom of priests, and a holy nation.

question: What signs accompanied God when he came down on Mount Sinai?
answer: Thunder, lightning, smoke, and a loud trumpet blast accompanied God when he came down.

question: What would God do to the Israelites if they disobeyed his commandments?
answer: He would punish them.

question: What did God tell the Israelites to build for him?
answer: He told them to make the Tent of Meeting.

question: Who could enter into the room behind the curtain where God was?
answer: Only the high priest could enter there.

question: How could the people cover their sin?
answer: They could bring an animal for the priests to sacrifice. The blood of the sacrifice would cover their sin.

question: Who did God choose to be his priests?
answer: He chose Aaron and his descendants.

question: What did the people do when they got tired of waiting for Moses to return from Mount Sinai?
answer: They asked Aaron to make a gold idol, and then they worshiped it and made sacrifices to it.

question: Why did God not destroy the Israelites when they disobeyed?
answer: He did not destroy them because Moses prayed for them.

question: What happened to the stones on which God had written the Ten Commandments?
answer: Moses was angry and smashed the stones.

question: What did Moses do to the idol?
answer: He burned the idol and ground it into powder, and then he made the people drink it in water.

question: Where did the Israelites go after Mount Sinai?
answer: God led the Israelites toward the Promised Land.

question: Where did God lead the Israelites after they left Mount Sinai?
answer: He led them towards Canaan, the Promised Land.

question: What did God tell the Israelites to do to the Canaanites?
answer: He told them to get rid of all of them, not to make peace with them, not to marry them, and to destroy all of their idols.

question: What did the 12 spies say about the land of Canaan?
answer: The land is very fertile and the crops are plentiful.

question: Why did ten of the spies say the Israelites should not attack the people of Canaan?
answer: They said, “The cities are strong and the people are giants. If we attack them, they will defeat us and kill us!”

question: What did Caleb and Joshua say about the people of Canaan?
answer: They said, “The people are strong, but we can defeat them. God will fight for us!”

question: What did the people want to do after they heard the report of the spies?
answer: They wanted to choose another leader and go back to Egypt.

question: How did God say he would punish the people for their disobedience?
answer: They would wander in the wilderness until everyone twenty years or older, except Caleb and Joshua, died.

question: Why were the Israelites defeated when they attacked the Canaanites?
answer: They were defeated because God did not go with them into the battle.

question: How long did the Israelites wander in the wilderness?
answer: They wandered for 40 years.

question: How did God provide for the Israelites in the wilderness?
answer: He gave them manna, sent flocks of quail, and kept their clothes and shoes from wearing out.

question: How did God respond when the people complained and grumbled?
answer: God was still faithful to his promises to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

question: Why was God angry when Moses struck the rock?
answer: God was angry because Moses dishonored God by not speaking to the rock as God told him to do.

question: How did God punish Moses for his disobedience?
answer: God said that Moses would not enter the Promised Land.

question: Who did God promise to send one day in the future?
answer: He would send another prophet like Moses.

question: Who led the Israelites after Moses died?
answer: Joshua led them.

question: What kind of leader was Joshua?
answer: He was a good leader because he trusted and obeyed God.

question: When it was time to enter the Promised Land, what did Joshua do first?
answer: He sent two spies to Jericho.

question: What did the spies promise to do for Rahab the prostitute?
answer: They promised to protect Rahab and her family when the Israelites destroyed the city.

question: How were the Israelites able to cross the Jordan River?
answer: When the priests started to step into the Jordan River, the water stopped flowing.

question: How did the Israelites attack Jericho?
answer: They marched around the city once a day for six days.

question: What did the Israelites do to Jericho on the seventh day?
answer: On the seventh day, they marched around the city seven more times. After they marched around the city for the last time, the priests blew their trumpets and the soldiers shouted.

question: What happened when the soldiers shouted and the priests blew trumpets?
answer: The walls of Jericho fell down so the Israelites could destroy everything in the city.

question: What happened to Rahab and her family?
answer: They were not killed, and they became part of the Israelites.

question: How did the Gibeonites trick the Israelites into making a peace treaty with them?
answer: They said they were from a place far from Canaan.

question: Why did Joshua and the Israelites not know the Gibeonites were lying?
answer: They did not ask God.

question: Why did the Israelites keep the peace treaty and defend the Gibeonites?
answer: They did not kill them because the Israelites had made a promise before God.

question: How else did God fight for the Israelites against the Amorites?
answer: He confused the Amorites and sent large hailstones on them.

question: How else did God fight for the Israelites against the Amorites?
answer: He caused the sun to stay in one place so the Israelites had enough time to completely defeat them.

question: What did Joshua and the Israelites do to the other Canaanite people groups who attacked them?
answer: Joshua and the Israelites destroyed them.

question: What did each tribe of Israel receive?
answer: God gave each of the 12 tribes of Israel its own section of the Promised Land.

question: Why did Joshua call the Israelites together when he was old?
answer: He called them together to remind them of their obligation to obey the covenant that God had made with them.

question: How did the Israelites answer Joshua?
answer: They promised to remain faithful to God and to follow his laws.

question: How did the Israelites disobey God after Joshua died?
answer: They did not drive out the Canaanites, and they worshiped the Canaanite gods instead of Yahweh, the true God.

question: How did God punish the Israelites for their disobedience?
answer: God allowed their enemies to defeat them.

question: How did God respond when the Israelites cried out for help?
answer: He provided a deliverer who rescued them and brought peace to the land.

question: What was Gideon doing when the angel of Yahweh came to him?
answer: Gideon was threshing grain secretly so the Midianites would not steal it.

question: What two signs did God do to prove that he would save Israel through Gideon?
answer: God made the morning dew fall only on the sheepskin and not the ground, and then the dew fell only on the ground and not the sheepskin.

question: Why did Gideon send home all except 300 of the soldiers?
answer: He sent them home because God told him he had too many men.

question: What additional sign did God give Gideon so he would not be afraid?
answer: Gideon heard a Midianite soldier tell of his dream that Gideon’s army would defeat the Midianite army.

question: What did Gideon do when he heard the Midianite soldier’s dream?
answer: He worshiped God.

question: How did Gideon and his men attack the Midianites?
answer: They surrounded the Midianite camp, broke their pots to reveal their torches, and blew their horns and shouted, “A sword for Yahweh and for Gideon.”

question: What did God do to help Gideon defeat the Midianites?
answer: God confused the Midianites so they attacked and killed each other.

question: What did Gideon do that later led the people to return to idol worship?
answer: He made a special garment of gold that the people later began to worship as an idol.

question: What did the Israelites do many times?
answer: The Israelites would sin, God would punish them, they would repent, and God would send a deliverer to save them.

question: Why did the people ask God for a king?
answer: All the other nations had kings, and the Israelites wanted someone to lead them into battle.

question: How did God answer their request?
answer: He gave them a king, just as they had asked.

question: Was Saul, the first king of Israel, a good king or a wicked king?
answer: He was good for the first few years, but then he became wicked.

question: What was David’s occupation before he became king?
answer: He was a shepherd who took care of sheep.

question: Why was it so amazing that David was able to kill Goliath?
answer: Goliath was a very tall, very strong trained soldier wearing battle gear. David was a shepherd boy with no weapon but a sling.

question: Why did the people of Israel praise David?
answer: He won many victories over Israel’s enemies.

question: What did David do when he had a chance to kill Saul in the cave?
answer: He spared Saul and only cut off a piece of his clothes.

question: What was the city that David conquered and then made his capital?
answer: He made Jerusalem his capital.

question: What did David want to build for God?
answer: David wanted to build a temple where all the Israelites could worship God and offer sacrifices.

question: Why did God not allow David to build a temple?
answer: David would not build it because he had fought in so many wars.

question: Who did God say would build the Temple?
answer: David’s son would build it.

question: What was the great promise that God gave to David?
answer: God promised that one of David’s descendants would rule as king over God’s people forever.

question: What great act would the Messiah do?
answer: He would save the people of the world from their sin.

question: What terrible sin did David commit later in his life?
answer: He committed adultery with Bathsheba, and murdered her husband.

question: What did David do so that people would not know that he had sinned?
answer: He had his general place Uriah where he would be killed in battle.

question: What did David do when Nathan confronted him about his sin?
answer: David repented of his sin and received God’s forgiveness.

question: How did God punish David for his sin?

question: What did the disciples think Jesus meant when he said that Lazarus had fallen asleep?
answer: They thought he was just asleep and would get better.

question: What did Jesus plainly tell the disciples about Lazarus?
answer: Jesus said that Lazarus had died.

question: Why was Jesus glad that he was not there when Lazarus died?
answer: Jesus was glad because something would happen that would make the disciples believe in him.

question: How long had Lazarus been dead?
answer: He had been dead for four days.

question: Did Martha believe that Jesus could have healed Lazarus?
answer: Yes, she believed that he could.

question: What will happen to believers because Jesus is the Resurrection and the Life?
answer: Whoever believes in Jesus will live, even though he dies, and everyone who believes in Jesus will never die.

question: Who did Martha believe that Jesus was?
answer: She believed he was the Messiah, the Son of God.

question: How long had Lazarus been dead?
answer: He had been dead for four days.

question: Why did Jesus thank the Father out loud?
answer: He did that so the people would believe that the Father had sent him.

question: What did Jesus command Lazarus to do?
answer: He commanded Lazarus to come out of the tomb!

question: How did the religious leaders of the Jews react when they saw the miracle?
answer: They envied Jesus and planned to kill him and Lazarus.

question: What was the meaning of Passover that the Jews celebrated every year?
answer: The Passover was a celebration of how God had freed the ancestors of the Jews from slavery in Egypt.

question: What did Judas want in exchange for betraying Jesus to the Jewish leaders?
answer: He offered to betray Jesus in exchange for money.

question: How much did the Jewish leaders pay Judas to betray Jesus?
answer: They paid him 30 silver coins.

question: At the Passover meal, what did Jesus say about the bread?
answer: He said, “This is my body, which is given for you.”

question: What did Jesus say about the cup?
answer: He said, “It is my blood of the New Covenant that I will pour out so that God will forgive your sins.”

question: Who did Jesus say would betray him?
answer: Jesus said the one to whom he would give the bread would betray him.

question: What happened to Judas after he took the bread from Jesus?
answer: Satan entered into Judas.

question: What did Jesus predict would happen to the disciples that night?
answer: He said they would all abandon him.

question: What did Jesus say that Peter would do before the rooster crowed?
answer: He said that Peter would deny three times that he knew Jesus.

question: How did the disciples respond to Jesus’ predictions about them?
answer: They said that they would die rather than deny Jesus.

question: What did Jesus pray to his Father at Gethsemane?
answer: He asked his Father not to make him drink the cup of suffering, but for God’s will to be done if there was no other way for people’s sins to be forgiven.

question: What were the disciples doing while Jesus prayed?
answer: They were sleeping.

question: How did the soldiers know which person was Jesus?
answer: Judas kissed Jesus as a sign for them to arrest him.

question: What did Peter do in order to defend Jesus?
answer: He pulled out a sword and cut off the ear of a servant of the high priest.

question: Why did Jesus say that he did not need Peter to defend him?
answer: Jesus said he could ask the Father for an army of angels.

question: What did the disciples do after Jesus was arrested?
answer: They all ran away.

question: What time of the day was it when the Jewish leaders began to question Jesus?
answer: It was the middle of the night.

question: Why could the Jewish leaders not prove Jesus was guilty of anything?
answer: The statements of the false witnesses did not agree with each other.

question: What question did the high priest finally ask Jesus?
answer: He asked Jesus, “Are you the Messiah, the Son of the living God?”

question: What answer did Jesus give to the high priest?
answer: Jesus said, “I am, and you will see me seated with God and coming from heaven.”

question: What was the crime that the high priest said that Jesus had committed?
answer: He said that Jesus had claimed he was the Son of God.

question: Where was Peter during Jesus’ trial?
answer: Peter was waiting outside the house of the high priest.

question: Why did the people think that Peter had been with Jesus?
answer: Peter and Jesus were both from Galilee.

question: What did Peter say when the people asked if he knew Jesus?
answer: Peter denied three times that he knew Jesus.

question: What happened immediately after Peter denied Jesus the third time?
answer: A rooster crowed, and Jesus turned and looked at Peter.

question: What did Judas do when he saw that the Jewish leaders had condemned Jesus?
answer: Judas became full of sorrow and went away and killed himself.

question: Why did the Jewish leaders take Jesus to the Roman governor Pilate?
answer: They wanted Pilate to condemn Jesus and kill him because they didn’t have the authority to do it themselves.

question: What was the first question that Pilate asked Jesus?
answer: He asked, “Are you the king of the Jews?”

question: What did Jesus say was the reason he came to earth?
answer: Jesus said he came to earth to tell the truth about God.

question: How many times did Pilate say to the crowd that Jesus was not guilty?
answer: He said three times that Jesus was not guilty.

question: If he believed Jesus was innocent, why did Pilate allow Jesus to be crucified?
answer: Pilate became afraid that the crowd would begin to riot.

question: How did the Roman soldiers treat Jesus?
answer: They whipped Jesus, put a royal robe and a crown of thorns on him, and mocked him.

question: When the soldiers led Jesus away to crucify him, what did they make him carry?
answer: They made him carry the cross on which he would die.

question: What was the name of the place where Jesus was crucified?
answer: It was called ‘the Skull.’

question: How did the soldiers attach Jesus to the cross?
answer: They nailed his hands and feet to the cross.

question: What did Jesus pray concerning the people who were crucifying him?
answer: He prayed, “Father, forgive them, because they do not know what they are doing.”

question: What was written on the sign above Jesus’ head?
answer: The sign said, “King of the Jews.”

question: How did the soldiers divide up Jesus’ clothes?
answer: They gambled for his clothing as had been prophesied.

question: What did the robber who did not mock Jesus ask him to do?
answer: He asked Jesus to remember him in his kingdom.

question: What was Jesus’ answer to the request of the robber?
answer: Jesus said, “Today, you will be with me in Paradise.”

question: What did the crowd want Jesus to do to prove that he was the Son of God?
answer: They told him to come down from the cross and save himself.

question: What unusual thing happened in the sky in the middle of the day?
answer: It became completely dark at noon and stayed dark for three hours.

question: What were the last words Jesus cried out from the cross?
answer: Jesus cried out, “It is finished! Father, I give my spirit into your hands.”

question: What miraculous things happened immediately after Jesus died?
answer: There was an earthquake and the large curtain in the Temple was torn in two, from top to bottom.

question: What did Jesus accomplish through his death?
answer: Jesus opened the way for people to come to God.

question: Who asked Pilate for Jesus’ body?
answer: Two Jewish leaders named Joseph and Nicodemus asked for his body.

question: What did they do with the body?
answer: They wrapped the body in cloth and placed it in a tomb cut out of rock, and then rolled a large stone in front of the tomb.

question: What did Jesus say would happen three days after his death?
answer: He would rise from the dead.

question: Did the Jewish leaders believe that Jesus would rise again?
answer: No, they thought he was lying.

question: What were the Jewish leaders afraid that the disciples would do?
answer: They thought the disciples would steal the body and say that Jesus had risen from the dead.

question: What did the Jewish leaders do to secure Jesus’ tomb?
answer: They put soldiers to guard the tomb and placed a seal on the stone at the entrance of the tomb.

question: When did the women go to Jesus’ tomb?
answer: They went there very early on the morning after the Sabbath day.

question: What miraculous events happened at the tomb before the women arrived there?
answer: There was an earthquake and an angel appeared, rolled away the stone, and sat on it.

question: What did the soldiers do when they saw that angel?
answer: They were terrified and fell to the ground like dead men.

question: What did the angel say to the women when they arrived at the tomb?
answer: The angel told them not to be afraid, for Jesus had risen from the dead. The angel told them to look in the tomb and see.

question: What did the angel tell the women to say to the disciples?
answer: He told them to tell the disciples that Jesus has risen from the dead, and that he would go to Galilee ahead of them.

question: Who appeared to the women as they were on their way to speak to the disciples?
answer: Jesus appeared to them.

question: What did the women do when they saw Jesus?
answer: They bowed down at his feet.

question: What were the two disciples talking about as they walked along the road?
answer: They were talking about what had happened to Jesus.

question: Who did the two disciples think Jesus was when he approached them on the road?
answer: They thought he was a foreigner who did not know what had happened in Jerusalem.

question: What had the prophets said would happen to the Messiah?
answer: They had said the Messiah would suffer and die, but would rise again on the third day.

question: What was Jesus doing when the two disciples recognized him?
answer: He was breaking a loaf of bread and thanking God for it.

question: What did the two disciples do after Jesus left them?
answer: They returned to Jerusalem and told the other disciples that Jesus was alive and that they had seen him.

question: How did Jesus prove to the disciples that he was not a ghost?
answer: He took a piece of fish and ate it.

question: What enabled the disciples to understand God’s word?
answer: Jesus made them understand God’s word better.

question: What was the message that Jesus’ disciples were to proclaim?
answer: They would proclaim that everyone should repent so that God would forgive their sins.

question: Where were Jesus’ disciples to proclaim this message?
answer: They would proclaim it first in Jerusalem, and then go to all people groups everywhere.

question: How long did Jesus continue to appear to the disciples?
answer: He appeared to them for 40 days.

question: How big was the largest group of disciples that saw Jesus during this time?
answer: He appeared to more than 500 disciples at the same time.

question: What did Jesus command his disciples to go and do?
answer: He told them to go and make disciples of all people groups, baptizing them in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, and teaching them to obey everything he had commanded them.

question: Why did Jesus tell the disciples to wait in Jerusalem?
answer: They were to wait until the Father gave them power when the Holy Spirit came on them.

question: Where did Jesus go 40 days after his resurrection?
answer: He went up to heaven.

question: What did Jesus do when he arrived in heaven?
answer: He sat down at the right hand of God to rule over all things.

question: What were the disciples doing while they waited in Jerusalem?
answer: They constantly gathered together to pray.

question: When did the Jews celebrate Pentecost?
answer: They celebrated Pentecost every year, 50 days after the Passover.

question: What happened to the believers during the Pentecost after Jesus rose from the dead?
answer: There was a sound like a strong wind, and something like flames of fire appeared over their heads. They were filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak in other languages.

question: Why were the people in the crowd astonished?
answer: The people in the crowd were from many different countries, but they each heard the disciples speaking in their native language.

question: What did some of the people think was the reason the disciples were talking this way?
answer: They thought the disciples were drunk.

question: What did Peter say was causing them to speak these languages?
answer: Peter said God was pouring out his Spirit.

question: Who did Peter say was responsible for crucifying Jesus?
answer: He said the people in the crowd crucified Jesus.

question: How did Peter say Jesus became alive again?
answer: God raised him from the dead.

question: What caused the disciples to be able to speak in other languages?
answer: The Holy Spirit caused them to be able to speak in other languages.

question: What were the two things that Peter said God caused Jesus to become?
answer: He became Lord and Messiah.

question: How did the people respond to Peter’s message?
answer: They were deeply moved and asked, “Brothers, what should we do?”

question: What did Peter tell the people to do?
answer: He told them they needed God to forgive their sins, so they should repent and be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ.

question: How many people believed and were baptized that day?
answer: About 3,000 people believed.

question: What did the disciples spend their time doing?
answer: The disciples continually listened to the teaching of the apostles, spent time together, ate together, prayed with each other, praised God together, and shared everything.

question: What did the crippled man expect Peter and John to give him?
answer: He was begging for money.

question: What did Peter give to the lame man instead of money?
answer: In the name of Jesus, Peter told him to get up and walk.

question: What did Peter say caused the crippled man to be healed?
answer: He said Jesus healed the man with his power because Peter and John believed in Jesus.

question: Who did Peter say killed Jesus?
answer: He said the people in the crowd told the Roman governor to kill Jesus.

question: What prophecies did the people fulfill when they killed Jesus?
answer: The prophets said that the Messiah would suffer and die.

question: What did Peter tell the people that they should do?
answer: They should repent and turn to God, so that he would wash away their sins.

question: How many men believed in Jesus as a result of Peter’s message?
answer: About 5,000 men believed.

question: What did Peter say is the only way to be saved?
answer: He said the only way to be saved is through the power of Jesus.

question: Why were the Jewish leaders shocked at the preaching of Peter and John?
answer: Peter and John were ordinary, uneducated men.

question: What did the Jewish leaders finally decide to do with Peter and John?
answer: They threatened them and then let them go.

question: What do we learn about Stephen?
answer: Everyone respected him, and the Holy Spirit gave him much power and wisdom.

question: What was the false charge that some Jews brought against Stephen?
answer: They said they heard Stephen speak evil things about Moses and God.

question: What did Stephen say the people had done that was worse than their ancestors?
answer: They killed the Messiah.

question: How did the religious leaders react to Stephen’s accusation?
answer: They dragged Stephen out of the city and threw stones at him in order to kill him.

question: What was the last thing Stephen said before he died?
answer: The last thing he said was, “Master, do not hold this sin against them.”

question: What did the believers do when the persecution began in Jerusalem?
answer: They fled to other places and preached about Jesus wherever they went.

question: Who did Philip meet on the road in the wilderness?
answer: He met an important official from Ethiopia.

question: What was the Ethiopian official doing as Philip approached?
answer: He was reading what the prophet Isaiah wrote.

question: Did the official understand the prophecy that he was reading?
answer: No, he needed someone to explain it to him.

question: Who did Philip say Isaiah had written about?
answer: He said Isaiah had written about Jesus.

question: After Philip explained the prophecy and they came to some water, what did the Ethiopian ask Philip?
answer: The Ethiopian asked if he could be baptized.

question: What happened to Philip after he baptized the Ethiopian official?
answer: The Holy Spirit carried Philip away to another place.

question: What did the Ethiopian official do after Philip left him?
answer: He continued traveling toward his home, happy that he knew Jesus.

question: Why was Saul going to Damascus?
answer: He went there to arrest followers of Jesus and to bring them back to Jerusalem.

question: What question did Jesus ask Saul on the road to Damascus?
answer: He asked Saul, “Why are you persecuting me?”

question: What happened to Saul when he got up after seeing the bright light?
answer: Saul could not see. His friends led him into Damascus and he did not eat or drink for three days.

question: Why was Ananias afraid to speak to Saul?
answer: He had heard that Saul was persecuting the believers.

question: What did God say was the purpose for which he had chosen Saul?
answer: God had chosen Saul to declare God’s name to the Jews and to people from other people groups.

question: How did Ananias enable Saul to see again?
answer: He placed his hands on him.

question: What did Ananias do to Saul after he regained his sight?
answer: Ananias baptized him.

question: What message did Saul immediately begin preaching to the Jews?
answer: He preached, “Jesus is the Son of God!”

question: How did the Jews respond to Saul’s preaching?
answer: They made a plan to kill Saul.

question: How did Saul escape from Damascus?
answer: His friends lowered him over the city wall in a basket so he could escape.

question: Who helped Saul to be accepted by the disciples in Jerusalem?
answer: Barnabas took Saul to the apostles and told them how Saul had preached boldly in Damascus.

question: What was different about the people who became believers in Antioch?
answer: They were not Jews.

question: What name first began to be used for the believers in Antioch?
answer: They called them “Christians.”

question: What was the church in Antioch doing when the Holy Spirit told them to set apart Barnabas and Saul?
answer: They were praying and fasting.

question: What was the purpose for which the church in Antioch sent out Saul and Barnabas?
answer: They sent them out to preach the good news about Jesus in many other places.

question: What was the Roman name that Saul began to use?
answer: He began to use the name “Paul.”

question: Where did Paul and Silas go in Philippi to proclaim the good news about Jesus?
answer: They went to a place by the river outside the city where people gathered to pray.

question: What made it possible for Lydia to believe in Jesus?
answer: God enabled Lydia to understand the message about Jesus.

question: What did Paul and Silas do to Lydia after she believed?
answer: They baptized Lydia and her family.

question: What did the demon-possessed slave girl keep yelling when she saw Paul and Silas?
answer: She yelled, “These men are servants of the Most High God. They are telling you the way to be saved!”

question: How did Paul respond to the demon’s testimony?
answer: Paul commanded the demon to leave the slave girl.

question: Why were the owners of the slave girl angry that the demon was gone?
answer: They realized that people would no longer pay money to them for her to tell people the future.

question: What were Paul and Silas doing in the middle of the night in jail?
answer: They were singing songs of praise to God.

question: What happened while Paul and Silas were singing?
answer: There was a violent earthquake, the prison doors flew open, and the chains of the prisoners fell off.

question: Why was the jailer afraid?
answer: He thought all the prisoners had escaped, and that the Roman authorities would kill him for letting them go.

question: What question did the jailer ask Paul?
answer: He asked, “What must I do to be saved?”

question: What did Paul say the jailer had to do in order to be saved?
answer: Paul told him to believe in Jesus, the Master.

question: What happened to some of the letters Paul and other follower of Jesus leaders wrote to the believers in the churches?
answer: Some of these letters became books of the Bible.

question: What was the world like when God first created it?
answer: Everything was perfect, and there was no sin, sickness, or death.

question: Why does everyone on earth die?
answer: They die because Adam and Eve sinned against God.

question: What is the condition of every person who is born?
answer: They are enemies of God, and have no peace with him.

question: What does it mean that Satan will “wound the heel” of Eve’s descendent?
answer: Satan would kill the Messiah, but God would raise him to live again.

question: In what way is Jesus like the boat God provided when he destroyed the earth by the flood?
answer: God sent Jesus as a way to save people who believe in him.

question: How is Jesus different than the priests who came before him?
answer: He offered himself as the only sacrifice that could take away the sin of everyone.

question: How is God’s promise to Abraham fulfilled through Jesus?
answer: God considers everyone who believes in Jesus, from any people group, to be a descendant of Abraham.

question: How is Jesus like the ram that was sacrificed instead of Isaac?
answer: Jesus is the Lamb of God, who God gave to be a sacrifice in our place.

question: How is Jesus like the Passover Lamb?
answer: Jesus never sinned and there is nothing wrong with him, so his blood (his death) causes God to pass over and not punish anyone who believes in Jesus.

question: Who can be part of God’s people?
answer: Anyone from any people group can join God’s people through the New Covenant by believing in Jesus.

question: In what way is Jesus the greatest prophet of all?
answer: He is God, so all the things he did and said were the actions and words of God.

question: How does Jesus fulfill God’s promise to King David?
answer: Because Jesus is the Son of God, he is the descendant of David who can rule forever.

question: In what way is Jesus a greater king than David?
answer: Jesus is the king of the entire universe.

question: How is Jesus both God and human?
answer: Jesus became human because he was born of a woman. At the same time, he was and is God, and was born of virgin made pregnant by an act of the Holy Spirit.

question: How did Jesus prove that he is God?
answer: He did many miracles.

question: How should we love other people?
answer: We should love them in the same way as we love ourselves.

question: Who should we love more than anything else?
answer: We should love God more than anything else.

question: What is the most important thing for anyone?
answer: The most important thing is to belong to the kingdom of God.

question: What do people do when they reject the message about Jesus?
answer: They refuse to enter into his kingdom.

question: What does God want to do for sinners?
answer: He wants to forgive them and make them his children.

question: What does God hate?
answer: He hates sin.

question: What do we deserve from God because of our sin?
answer: We deserve to die.

question: What did God do to Jesus when he died on the cross?
answer: God punished Jesus for the sin of mankind, you and me.

question: Why was Jesus’ sacrifice able to take away the sins of every person in the world?
answer: Jesus could take away our sins because he never sinned and was the perfect sacrifice.

question: Who will God save?
answer: God will save everyone who believes in Jesus and accepts him as his Master.

question: If you are a follower of Jesus, are you still an enemy of God?
answer: No, you are now a close friend of God.

question: Are followers of Jesus still tempted to sin?
answer: Yes, they are tempted.

question: What should followers of Jesus do when they sin?
answer: They should confess their sins to God.

question: What does God promise to do if we confess our sins?
answer: He promises to forgive us, and to give us strength to fight against sin.

question: What are some of the things that God tells followers of Jesus to do?
answer: He tells us to pray, study his word, worship him, and tell others about what he has done for us.

question: During the last 2,000 years, what has happened to the number of people who believe in Jesus?
answer: The number has been increasing.

question: How does God want us to live as we wait for Jesus to return?
answer: He wants us to live in a way that is holy and that honors him.

question: What did Jesus say would happen before the end of the world comes?
answer: His disciples would preach the good news of the kingdom of God to people everywhere in the world.

question: How will the world that hated Jesus treat his disciples?
answer: The world will cause his disciples to suffer also.

question: What is God’s promise to those who remain faithful to the end?
answer: He promises that God will save them.

question: In Jesus’ story about the end of the world, how did the weeds come to be among the wheat?
answer: An enemy planted them.

question: Why didn’t the servants pull out the weeds?
answer: Their master did not want them to accidentally pull out the wheat along with the weeds.

question: What does the good seed represent?
answer: The good seed represents the people of God’s kingdom.

question: What does the harvest represent?
answer: The harvest represents the end of the world.

question: What will happen to the people who belong to the devil at the end of the world?
answer: The angels will gather them up and throw them into a very hot fire, where they will suffer terribly.

question: In what form will Jesus return to the earth?
answer: He will return the way that he left, with a real body, and on the clouds in the sky.

question: When Jesus returns, what will happen to every follower of Jesus who has died?
answer: They will also rise to meet him in the sky.

question: When Jesus returns, what will happen to the followers of Jesus who are still alive?
answer: The followers of Jesus who are alive will rise up into the sky and join with the other followers of Jesus who rose from the dead.

question: What will Jesus do to Satan when he returns?
answer: Jesus will throw Satan into hell, where he will burn forever.

question: What will life be like in the new heaven and new earth?
answer: Jesus will rule his kingdom justly and with peace, and there will be no more suffering.
